children: Micron (MU) secured 26 long-term supply deals covering over 35% of sales to 2030; backlog about $150B, ~$32B committed by customers, and >75% of fiscal 2027 output already booked.
Micron (MU) reported fiscal Q4 revenue of $54.229B, Cloud Memory operating margin 76%, Core Data Center margin 85%, and guided Q1 revenue $61.5B ± $1.5B (≈13.4% q/q).
Micron (MU) says data-center DRAM and HBM demand is strong. Taichung plant sold out for 2027. Company expects HBM to outpace DRAM and tight supply may persist into 2028.
Traders: Micron (MU) faces AI-driven memory demand vs. rising capacity. Customer orders hint at sustained demand through 2028–30, but near-term margin pressure and volatility persist.
Micron (MU) is up ~260% YTD. Cash and short-term investments exceed debt by about $68.3B. Hedge fund holders rose from 154 to 184, holding roughly $34.9B in shares.
Analyst Gil Luria raised Micron (MU) price target to $3,000 from $2,100, citing 26 long-term deals covering 35%+ of revenue through 2030 and significant contract-related deposits.
Elon Musk praised Micron (MU) on X for fair future memory pricing and use in xAI/SpaceX Colossus data centers with Nvidia GPUs. MU shares fell about 3.2% on Oct 14.
